recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed unless FHIR-I reopens SubscriptionTopic trigger/filter semantics; adding redundant prose now would risk drift from the maintained queryCriteria and FHIRPath sections.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive R5 FHIR-I issue asking SubscriptionTopic filtering timing text to distinguish server-defined trigger behavior from requester-specified Subscription filters, explain resultForCreate/resultForDelete query timing, clarify that query controls do not apply to FHIRPath trigger tests, and make clear that trigger tests are part of SubscriptionTopic evaluation.
initial_application: Commit 69f237bba9 applied the original FHIR-39028 change to source/subscriptiontopic/subscriptiontopic-notes.xml by adding Triggers vs. Filters narrative, a distinct FHIRPath timing paragraph, and query-specific create/delete/update timing guidance for resultForCreate/resultForDelete. Current source later refactored R5 resourceTrigger/eventTrigger terminology into SubscriptionTopic.trigger while preserving fhir.ini aliases.
additional_context: SubscriptionTopic is active in the current build through source/fhir.ini. The current narrative now explains topic-level trigger criteria, client filter options, queryCriteria previous/current behavior for create/delete/update, and separate FHIRPath %previous/%current inputs. FHIR-39025 and FHIR-50619 are same-family/later clarifications that refine resultForCreate/resultForDelete/requireBoth semantics without reversing FHIR-39028. FHIR-I minutes confirm the 9-0-0 motion, and Zulip searches found no direct conflicting discussion.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The existing SubscriptionTopic source already satisfies the Jira resolution after the original application, trigger refactor, and later R6 cleanup.
